captions.instagram:
How does the stomach digest food?

Your stomach is a muscular bag of acid strong enough to dissolve meat, yet it doesn't digest itself. Swallow a bolus, cut the stomach open, watch it churn food into chyme three times a minute, and meet the germ a doctor drank to win a Nobel Prize.

→ Food travels a 25 cm tube, the oesophagus, down into a J-shaped bag under your left ribs.
→ Cut open, the stomach’s lining is folded into ridges called rugae, wrapped in three layers of muscle.
→ When you swallow, a flap called the epiglottis seals your windpipe for about a second.
→ Then a squeeze wave carries food down the oesophagus. It even works upside down.
→ Parietal cells pump out hydrochloric acid, about as sour as lemon juice or stronger.

youtubeLong.title: How does the stomach digest food? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Your stomach is a muscular bag of acid strong enough to dissolve meat, yet it doesn't digest itself. Swallow a bolus, cut the stomach open, watch it churn food into chyme three times a minute, and meet the germ a doctor drank to win a Nobel Prize.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/stomachclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/stomachclear

In this video:
• A 25 cm tube and a J-shaped bag. Food goes from the mouth down the oesophagus, about 25 cm long, through the diaphragm into the stomach, which sits under the left ribs.
• Swallowing is a squeeze, not a slide. Chewing mixes food with saliva, whose amylase starts on starch.
• Acid that doesn't burn its maker. Parietal cells use proton pumps to make hydrochloric acid, keeping the stomach at about pH 1.5 to 3.5.
• A mill with a gatekeeper. About three times a minute a squeeze sweeps towards the pylorus, grinding food into chyme.
• Hungry, full and growling. The empty stomach holds about 75 mL but relaxes to take 1 to 1.5 litres.
• When things go wrong. Acid slipping past a weak sphincter causes heartburn.
